meta.purpose: Held-out test set. Run only for final reporting, never while tuning. Report separately from the development set (seed_questions.json).
meta.default_jurisdiction: UAE federal private sector (Federal Decree-Law 33/2021 as amended)
meta.authoring_note: Drafted by Claude Code on 2026-11-22 from the official text in data/processed/*.jsonl, before any retrieval or answer run on these questions. Caveat: the drafter had seen the development-set results, so this set is not fully blind. Owner reviews and edits it before the first run.
meta.coverage: Paraphrases of development topics with different wording, two- and three-article questions, gratuity above 5 years with a partial year, a premise trap (allowances), an under-one-year trap, partial coverage (minimum wage), out-of-corpus abstention (tax) and a second free-zone jurisdiction (ADGM).

source_status_legend.verified: Article text checked against the ingested official text.
source_status_legend.partially_verified: Some legal points are supported, but the question extends beyond the verified source coverage.

meta.note: Evaluation material for a software project. Not legal advice.

items.question: I finished my probation a while ago and I've been off ill for 20 days so far this year. How much of that time is paid?
required_facts: The first 15 days of sick leave are on full pay
The following 30 days are on half pay, so the remaining 5 of the 20 days are on half pay
The worker must notify the employer within 3 business days and submit a medical report
items.notes: Paraphrase of fact-01 using 'off ill' instead of 'sick leave'. Art. 31(4) (no pay if illness results from misconduct) is not required.

items.question: My wife just gave birth. Do I get any paid time off as the dad?
required_facts: Paid parental leave of 5 working days
Can be taken continuously or intermittently within 6 months of the child's birth
items.notes: Colloquial wording ('dad', 'time off'); the law says 'parental leave'. CR 1/2022 Art. 21(4) adds proof of birth; not a required fact. Must not answer with maternity leave.

items.question: My basic salary is AED 9,000 a month and I'm leaving after 7 and a half years with the same company. What end-of-service gratuity should I get?
items.calculation: First 5 years: 5 x 21 = 105 days. Remaining 2.5 years: 2.5 x 30 = 75 days. Total 180 days. Daily wage = 9,000 / 30 = 300. Gratuity = 180 x 300 = AED 54,000. Cap (two years' wage) not reached.
required_facts: 21 days of basic wage for each of the first five years
30 days of basic wage for each year after the first five
Parts of a year are paid in proportion to the time worked
items.notes: Gratuity above 5 years with a partial year. Assumes a foreign full-time worker, continuous service, no unpaid absence (Art. 51(4)) and no alternative savings scheme (Art. 51(8)). Art. 67: a month is 30 days.

items.question: I earn AED 20,000 a month in total: AED 12,000 basic plus AED 8,000 housing and transport allowances. I've worked here 3 years. How much gratuity will I get?
items.calculation: 3 x 21 = 63 days. Daily basic wage = 12,000 / 30 = 400. Gratuity = 63 x 400 = AED 25,200. Using the total salary would wrongly give AED 42,000.
required_facts: Gratuity is calculated on the basic wage only, not the allowances
21 days of basic wage for each of the first five years
items.notes: Premise trap: the question leads with the total salary. The tool must be called with 12,000, not 20,000.

items.question: I'm leaving after 10 months. My basic is AED 8,000. How much gratuity do I get?
required_facts: No end-of-service gratuity, because it requires at least one year of continuous service
Does not compute a pro-rata gratuity for the 10 months
items.notes: Trap: Art. 51(3) pays parts of a year pro rata only once one year is completed. No expected_value: the right answer is 'none', and the numeric check would only look for the digit 0. No 'calculation' key, so a tool call is not required.

items.question: I'm still on probation and another company in Dubai has offered me a job. How much notice do I have to give my current employer?
required_facts: At least one month's notice
The notice must be in writing
The new employer compensates the original employer for recruitment costs unless agreed otherwise
items.notes: Must not answer with the 14 days that apply when leaving the State (9(4)) or when the employer terminates (9(1)), nor with the 30-90 day rule of Art. 43. Assumes a mainland Dubai employer; DIFC would be out of scope.

items.question: My manager wants me to stay 3 extra hours every day. Is that allowed, and do I get paid more for it?
required_facts: Normal working hours are at most 8 per day or 48 per week
Overtime may not exceed 2 hours per day, except under conditions in the Executive Regulation
Total working hours may not exceed 144 hours every 3 weeks
Overtime is paid at the normal hourly wage based on the basic wage plus at least 25%
At least 50% extra for overtime between 10 pm and 4 am (shift workers excluded)
items.notes: Two-article question. The 10 pm-4 am fact checks that the answer is complete; the owner may drop it if it seems incidental (see the num-05 commuting-fact lesson).

items.question: My employer ended my contract (not for disciplinary reasons). I have paid into the unemployment insurance scheme for 18 months and my basic salary is AED 40,000. How much would I get each month, and for how long?
required_facts: Compensation is 60% of the subscription salary
Capped at AED 20,000 per month for this salary level (second category, subscription salary above AED 16,000), so AED 20,000 rather than AED 24,000
Paid for up to 3 months per claim
The claim must be submitted within 30 days of the end of employment

sources.doc: Federal Decree-Law No. 13 of 2022 concerning Insurance Against Unemployment

items.notes: Two-document question with a cap. 60% x 40,000 = 24,000, capped at 20,000. No calculator tool exists for this, so no 'calculation' key. Other conditions (premiums paid, legal residence, CR 97/2022 Art. 9) are not required facts.

items.question: How many days off do private-sector employees get for Eid al-Adha?
required_facts: Arafa Day (9 Dhu al-Hijjah) is 1 day
Eid Al-Adha is 3 days, 10 to 12 Dhu al-Hijjah
Does not present Gregorian dates as confirmed

sources.doc: Cabinet Resolution No. 27 of 2024 Concerning the Public Holidays in the State

items.notes: Answering '4 days' (Arafa + Eid) or listing them separately are both fine.

items.question: What is the minimum wage in the UAE?
required_facts: The Decree-Law lets the Cabinet set a minimum wage by resolution
Says its sources do not state a minimum wage amount, and does not invent one
items.notes: Partial coverage: the enabling article is in the corpus, but no figure is. Tests hallucination of a number.

items.question: How much income tax will be deducted from my salary?
required_facts: Says tax is not covered by its employment-law sources
Does not state a tax rate or amount
items.notes: Out-of-corpus abstention. Nothing in data/processed mentions income tax.

items.question: I work for a company registered in ADGM. What notice period do I have to give?
required_facts: Says its sources cover UAE federal private-sector law only, not ADGM
Does not give the federal 30-90 day rule as if it applied to ADGM
items.notes: Second free-zone jurisdiction (development set only tests DIFC).
